translations.literal: Biography 58: Imperial Affines — Shi Jianu, Pei Manda, Hu Du, Tudan Gong, Wugulun Puluhu, Tangkuo Dewen, Wugulun Zhanmeihe, Pucha Ahudie, Wulin Dahui, Pucha Dingshou, Tudan Sizhong, Tudan Yi, Wulin Dafu, Wugulun Yuanzhong's son Yi, Tangkuo Gong, Wulin Dalin, Tudan Gongbi, Tudan Ming, Tudan Sixi
translations.idiomatic: Biography 58: Imperial Affines — Shi Jianu, Pei Manda, Hu Du, Tudan Gong, Wugulun Puluhu, Tangkuo Dewen, Wugulun Zhanmeihe, Pucha Ahudie, Wulin Dahui, Pucha Dingshou, Tudan Sizhong, Tudan Yi, Wulin Dafu, Yi (son of Wugulun Yuanzhong), Tangkuo Gong, Wulin Dalin, Tudan Gongbi, Tudan Ming, and Tudan Sixi

sentences.zh: 金昭祖娶徒單氏，后妃之族，自此始見。

translations.literal: The Jin Founder Zhaozu married a woman of the Tudan clan; the families of empresses and consorts first appear in the records from this time.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin dynastic founder Zhaozu took a wife from the Tudan clan, the kin of empresses and imperial consorts first entered the historical record.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，烏春為難，世祖欲求昏以結其歡心，烏春曰：「女直與胡里改豈可為昏。

translations.literal: During Shizu's time, Wuchun caused trouble; Shizu wished to form a marriage alliance to win his favor. Wuchun said: "How can Jurchens and the Holi clan intermarry?"
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Shizu, Wuchun stirred up trouble, and Shizu sought a marriage tie to win him over. Wuchun replied, "How could Jurchens and the Holi people ever marry one another?"

sentences.zh: 」世宗時，賜夾穀清臣族同國人。

translations.literal: During Shizong's time, the Jiagu Qingchen clan was granted the status of fellow-countrymen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong, the Jiagu Qingchen clan was granted the same standing as native Jin subjects.

sentences.zh: 清臣，胡里改人也。

translations.literal: Qingchen was a man of the Holi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen himself came from the Holi people.

sentences.zh: 然則四十七部之中亦有不通昏因者矣，其故則莫能詰也。

translations.literal: Thus even among the forty-seven tribes there were some between whom marriage alliance was not permitted, but the reason cannot be ascertained.
translations.idiomatic: So even among the forty-seven tribes there were groups that did not intermarry, though the reason can no longer be traced.

sentences.zh: 有國家者，昏因有恆族，能使風氣淳固，親義不渝，而貴賤等威有別焉，蓋良法也歟。

translations.literal: For a state, having fixed marriage-alliance clans can make customs pure and solid, kinship obligations unchanging, and distinctions of noble and base, superior and inferior — is this not a fine method?
translations.idiomatic: For any polity, fixed marriage clans can keep customs wholesome and kinship bonds steady, while preserving distinctions of rank and dignity — surely that is sound policy.

sentences.zh: 作《世戚傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore the "Biographies of Imperial Affines" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this "Biographies of Imperial Affines" was written.

sentences.zh: 石家奴

translations.literal: Shi Jianu
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jianu

sentences.zh: 石家奴，蒲察部人，世居案出虎水。

translations.literal: Shi Jianu was a man of the Pucha tribe; his family had long lived by the Ansuchu River.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jianu belonged to the Pucha tribe and his lineage had long settled on the Ansuchu River.

sentences.zh: 祖斛魯短，世祖外孫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huluhan was a maternal grandson of Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huluhan was Shizu's grandson on the maternal side.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達之亂，昭肅皇后父母兄弟皆在敵境，斛魯短以計迎還之。

translations.literal: During the disorders of Huanzan and Sandai, the parents and brothers of Empress Zhaosu were all in enemy territory; Huluhan brought them back by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: In the upheavals of Huanzan and Sandai, Empress Zhaosu's parents and brothers were all trapped in hostile territory, and Huluhan contrived to bring them safely back.

sentences.zh: 石家奴自幼時撫養于太祖家，及長，太祖以女妻之。

translations.literal: Shi Jianu was reared in Taizu's household from childhood; when grown, Taizu gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jianu was raised in Taizu's household from boyhood, and when he came of age Taizu gave him a princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 年十五，從攻甯江州，敗遼主親軍，攻臨潢府皆有功，襲謀克。

translations.literal: At fifteen he followed the attack on Ningjiang Prefecture, defeated the Liao emperor's personal guard, and had merit in the assault on Linhuang Prefecture; he inherited the position of meng'an commander.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he joined the assault on Ningjiang, routed the Liao emperor's personal guard, distinguished himself at Linhuang, and inherited his father's meng'an command.

sentences.zh: 其後，自山西護齊國王謀良虎之喪歸上京，道由興中。

translations.literal: Afterward, while escorting the coffin of Prince Qi Guowang Moulianghu back from Shanxi to Shangjing, he passed through Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while escorting Prince Qi Guowang Moulianghu's coffin from Shanxi back to Shangjing, he traveled by way of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 是時，方攻興中未下，石家奴置柩于驛，率其所領猛安兵助王師，遂破其城。

translations.literal: At that time the attack on Xingzhong had not yet succeeded; Shi Jianu left the coffin at the relay station, led his meng'an troops to aid the imperial army, and thus captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Xingzhong was still unresolved; Shi Jianu left the bier at the post station, led his meng'an soldiers to reinforce the imperial forces, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 從宗望討張覺。

translations.literal: He followed Zongwang in the campaign against Zhang Jue.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned under Zongwang against Zhang Jue.

sentences.zh: 再從宗翰伐宋。

translations.literal: Again he followed Zonghan in the invasion of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Zonghan in the campaign against Song.

sentences.zh: 宗翰聞宗望軍已圍汴，遣石家奴計事，抵平定軍遇敵兵數萬，敗之，遂見宗望。

translations.literal: Zonghan heard that Zongwang's army had already surrounded Bianjing; he sent Shi Jianu to confer on affairs. Reaching Pingding Army he encountered tens of thousands of enemy troops, defeated them, and then saw Zongwang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zongwang's forces had already invested Bianjing, Zonghan dispatched Shi Jianu to coordinate plans. At Pingding Army he met a Song force tens of thousands strong, routed it, and then joined Zongwang.

sentences.zh: 已還報，宗翰聞其平定之戰，甚嘉之。

translations.literal: After he returned with his report, Zonghan heard of his victory at Pingding and greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned with his report, Zonghan heard of the victory at Pingding and commended him highly.

sentences.zh: 明年，復伐宋，石家奴隸婁室軍。

translations.literal: The next year he again invaded Song; Shi Jianu was assigned to Lou Shi's army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in another Song campaign, Shi Jianu served under Lou Shi.

sentences.zh: 婁室討陝西未下，石家奴領所部兵援之。

translations.literal: Lou Shi had not yet subdued Shaanxi; Shi Jianu led his own troops to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Shi had not yet pacified Shaanxi, and Shi Jianu marched his command to his aid.

sentences.zh: 既而，以本部屯戍西京，會契丹大石出奔，以余睹為元帥，石家奴為副，襲諸部族以還。

translations.literal: Before long he garrisoned his command at the western capital with his own unit; when the Khitan Yelü Dashi fled, Yuduo was made commander-in-chief and Shi Jianu deputy; they raided the various tribes and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then garrisoned his unit at the Western Capital. When the Khitan prince Dashi fled, Yuduo was made supreme commander with Shi Jianu as his deputy; they raided the tribal domains and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有疾，退居鄉里。

translations.literal: Not long after he fell ill and retired to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill and retired to his native place.

sentences.zh: 天眷間，授侍中、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: During the Tianjuan era he was appointed Director of Palace Affairs and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjuan period he was made Director of Palace Affairs and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.

sentences.zh: 再以都統定邊部，熙宗賜御書嘉獎之。

translations.literal: He was again made supreme commander to pacify the frontier tribes; Xizong bestowed imperial writing in praise of him.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed supreme commander to settle the frontier tribes, and Xizong rewarded him with an imperial commendation in the emperor's own hand.

sentences.zh: 封蘭陵郡王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 除東京留守，以病致仕。

translations.literal: Appointed military governor of the eastern capital; he retired on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of the Eastern Capital but retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十三，加贈鄖王。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-three; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-three and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.

sentences.zh: 正隆奪王爵，封魯國公。

translations.literal: Under Zhenglong his princely title was revoked and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenglong his princely rank was stripped and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 裴滿達

translations.literal: Pei Manda
translations.idiomatic: Pei Manda

sentences.zh: 忽睹，天眷三年權猛安，皇統元年為行軍猛安。

translations.literal: Hu Du — in Tianjuan 3 acting meng'an; in Huangtong 1 marching meng'an commander.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Du served as acting meng'an commander in the third year of Tianjuan and as marching meng'an commander in the first year of Huangtong.

sentences.zh: 曆橫海、崇義軍節度使，以後戚怙勢贓汙不法。

translations.literal: He successively served as military governor of Henghai and Chongyi circuits, and as an imperial affine relied on his position to commit corruption and unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive posts as military governor of Henghai and Chongyi, and as a maternal kinsman of the throne he abused his power with brazen corruption.

sentences.zh: 其在橫海，拜富人為父，及死，為之行服而分其資。

translations.literal: While at Henghai he acknowledged a rich man as his father; when the man died he wore mourning for him and divided his estate.
translations.idiomatic: At Henghai he took a wealthy man as his adoptive father; when the man died he donned mourning garb and carved up his property.

sentences.zh: 在崇義，諷寺僧設齋而受其施。

translations.literal: At Chongyi he urged temple monks to hold feasts and accepted their offerings.
translations.idiomatic: At Chongyi he induced temple monks to hold banquets and pocketed their donations.

sentences.zh: 及留守中京，益驕恣，苟可以得財無不為者。

translations.literal: When he became military governor of the central capital he grew still more arrogant and unrestrained; whatever might yield profit he would do.
translations.idiomatic: As military governor of the Central Capital he grew still more arrogant, stopping at nothing that might turn a profit.

sentences.zh: 選諸猛安富人子弟為紮野，規取財物，時號「閑郎君」。

translations.literal: He selected sons of rich men from the various meng'an as his attendants to extort goods and wealth; people at the time called them the "Idle Young Lords."
translations.idiomatic: He recruited sons of wealthy meng'an families as personal attendants to squeeze them for goods and cash, and contemporaries dubbed them the "Idle Young Lords."

sentences.zh: 朝廷以忽睹與徒單恭等汙濫至甚，命秉德黜陟天下官吏，忽睹以贓罷。

translations.literal: Because Hu Du and Tudan Gong and others had been so extremely corrupt, the court ordered Bingde to promote and demote officials throughout the realm; Hu Du was dismissed for bribery.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Hu Du, Tudan Gong, and others to have sunk to extreme corruption and charged Bingde with reviewing officials empire-wide; Hu Du was removed for graft.

sentences.zh: 海陵以忽睹所至縱家奴擾民，乃定禁外官任所閒雜人條約。

translations.literal: Hailing, because wherever Hu Du went he let his household slaves harass the people, established regulations forbidding idle hangers-on at the posts of officials outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hu Du had allowed his household slaves to harass the populace wherever he served, Hailing promulgated rules barring superfluous retainers from provincial official residences.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，復起為鄭州防禦使，改安國軍節度使。

translations.literal: In Tiande 3 he was reappointed Defender of Zhengzhou, then transferred to military governor of Anguo circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiande he was recalled as Defender of Zhengzhou and later transferred to military governor of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: He died at thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 徒單恭

translations.literal: Tudan Gong
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Gong

sentences.zh: 徒單恭，本名斜也。

translations.literal: Tudan Gong — his original name was Xieye.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Gong, whose original name was Xieye.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，為奉國上將軍。

translations.literal: In Tianjuan 2 he was made General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjuan he was appointed General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 以告吳十反事，超授龍虎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: For reporting Wu Shi's rebellion he was exceptionally promoted to General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For exposing Wu Shi's conspiracy he was abruptly promoted to General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 為戶部侍郎，出為濟南尹，遷會甯牧，封譚國公。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of Revenue, went out as Prefect of Jinan, was transferred to Chief of Huining, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Minister of Revenue, was posted as Prefect of Jinan, then transferred to Chief of Huining and enfeoffed as Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 復出為太原尹。

translations.literal: He was again posted out as Prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent out as Prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 斜也貪鄙，使工繪一佛像，自稱嘗見佛，其像如此，當以金鑄之。

translations.literal: Xieye was greedy and base; he had artisans paint a Buddha image, claiming he had once seen the Buddha and that the image was like this and should be cast in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye was grasping and mean. He had craftsmen paint a Buddha image, claiming he had once seen the Buddha and that it should be cast in gold exactly as depicted.

sentences.zh: 遂賦屬縣金，而未嘗鑄佛，盡入其家，百姓號為「金總管」。

translations.literal: He then levied gold on the subordinate counties but never cast the Buddha; it all went into his household, and the people called him the "Gold Intendant."
translations.idiomatic: He levied gold from the counties under him but never cast the statue; everything went into his own coffers, and the people nicknamed him the "Gold Intendant."

sentences.zh: 秉德廉訪官吏，斜也以贓免。

translations.literal: When Bingde conducted an integrity inspection of officials, Xieye was dismissed for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: During Bingde's integrity review of officials, Xieye was removed for corruption.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，海陵後徒單氏，斜也女，由是復用為會甯牧，封王。

translations.literal: When Hailing seized the throne, Empress Tudan of Hailing was Xieye's daughter; for this reason he was again employed as Chief of Huining and enfeoffed as prince.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing usurped the throne, his empress Tudan was Xieye's daughter, and on that account he was restored as Chief of Huining and enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜平章政事，海陵獵于胡剌渾水，斜也編列圍場，凡平日不相能者輒杖之。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Councilor; when Hailing hunted on the Hulahun River, Xieye arranged the hunting enclosure and beat with rods anyone with whom he was not on good terms in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand Councilor. When Hailing hunted on the Hulahun River, Xieye laid out the beat and had anyone he disliked flogged on the spot.

sentences.zh: 海陵謂宰相曰：「斜也為相，朕非私之。

translations.literal: Hailing said to the chief ministers: "In making Xieye a councilor I am not showing favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing told the chief ministers, "I did not make Xieye a councilor out of private favor.

sentences.zh: 今聞軍國大事凡斜也所言，卿等一無取，豈千慮無一得乎？

translations.literal: Now I hear that on military and state affairs, whatever Xieye says, you take none of it — can it be that in a thousand deliberations there is not one that hits the mark?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear that on matters of war and state you reject everything he says. Can a man who deliberates a thousand times never once be right?"

sentences.zh: 」他宰相無以對，溫都思忠舉數事對曰：「某事本當如此，斜也輒以為如彼，皆妄生異議，不達事宜。

translations.literal: The other chief ministers had nothing to reply; Wendusi Zhong cited several matters and answered: "Such-and-such an affair ought to have been thus, but Xieye always insisted it should be otherwise — all were groundless objections born of contrariness, failing to grasp what the situation required.
translations.idiomatic: The other chief ministers had no answer. Wendusi Zhong cited several cases: "This matter should have been handled one way, yet Xieye always insisted on another — empty objections that showed he did not understand affairs at all.

sentences.zh: 臣逮事康宗，累朝宰相未嘗有如斜也專恣者。

translations.literal: Your servant has served since Emperor Kangzong; through successive reigns there has never been a chief minister as willful and overbearing as Xieye."
translations.idiomatic: I have served since the reign of Kangzong, and through successive reigns I have never seen a chief minister as domineering as Xieye."

sentences.zh: 」海陵默然。

translations.literal: Hailing fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 斜也於都堂脊杖令史馮仲尹，御史臺劾之，海陵杖之二十。

translations.literal: Xieye had the clerk Feng Zhongyin beaten on the back at the chief council chamber; the Censorate impeached him, and Hailing had him beaten twenty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye had the clerk Feng Zhongyin flogged across the back in the chief council hall. The Censorate impeached him, and Hailing ordered twenty strokes of the rod.

sentences.zh: 斜也猛安部人撒合出者，言斜也強率取部人財物。

translations.literal: Sahechu, a man of Xieye's meng'an tribe, said that Xieye had forcibly taken the property of tribesmen.
translations.idiomatic: Sahechu, a tribesman of Xieye's meng'an, accused him of forcibly seizing his clansmen's property.

sentences.zh: 海陵命侍御史保魯鞫之。

translations.literal: Hailing ordered Attending Censor Baolu to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing ordered Attending Censor Baolu to conduct the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 保魯鞫不以實，海陵杖保魯，而以撒合出為符寶祗候，改隸合紮猛安。

translations.literal: Baolu did not investigate according to the facts; Hailing had Baolu beaten and made Sahechu Keeper of Seals and Credentials, transferring him to the Hezha meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Baolu failed to investigate honestly, so Hailing had him beaten and appointed Sahechu Keeper of Seals and Credentials, reassigning him to the Hezha meng'an.

sentences.zh: 斜也兄定哥尚太祖長女兀魯，定哥死無子，以季弟之子查剌為後。

translations.literal: Xieye's elder brother Dingge had married Taizu's eldest daughter Wulu; Dingge died without sons, and the son of the youngest brother, Zhala, was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye's elder brother Dingge had married Taizu's eldest daughter Wulu. When Dingge died childless, the son of their youngest brother, Zhala, was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 斜也謀取其兄家財，強納兀魯為室而不相能，兀魯嘗怨詈斜也。

translations.literal: Xieye plotted to seize his brother's family wealth; he forced Wulu to marry him though they could not get along, and Wulu often cursed Xieye in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye schemed to seize his brother's estate, forced Wulu to marry him though they were incompatible, and Wulu often reviled him in anger.

sentences.zh: 斜也妾忽撻與兀魯不葉，乃譖兀魯於海陵後徒單氏曰：「兀魯怨上殺其兄宗敏，有怨望語。

translations.literal: Xieye's concubine Hutà did not get along with Wulu; she slandered Wulu to Empress Tudan of Hailing, saying: "Wulu resents the emperor for killing her brother Zongmin and has spoken words of resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Xieye's concubine Hutà quarreled with Wulu and slandered her to Empress Tudan, claiming that Wulu resented the emperor for executing her brother Zongmin and had uttered disloyal words.

sentences.zh: 」會韓王亨改廣甯尹，諸公主宗婦往賀其母，兀魯以言慰亨母，忽撻亦以怨望指斥誣兀魯。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince Han Xian was transferred to be Prefect of Guangning; the various princesses and clanswomen went to congratulate his mother. Wulu spoke words of consolation to Xian's mother, but Hutà also accused Wulu of resentment and slander.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Xian was reassigned as Prefect of Guangning, the imperial princesses and clanswomen went to congratulate his mother. Wulu offered words of comfort to the prince's mother, but Hutà again accused her of disloyalty and slander.

sentences.zh: 海陵使蕭裕鞫之，忽撻得幸于徒單後，左驗皆不敢言，遂殺兀魯，斜也因而盡奪查剌家財。

translations.literal: Hailing had Xiao Yu investigate; Hutà enjoyed favor with Empress Tudan, and corroborating witnesses all dared not speak; Wulu was therefore killed, and Xieye thereby seized all of Zhala's family property.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had Xiao Yu conduct the inquiry. Hutà enjoyed the empress's favor, witnesses dared not testify honestly, and Wulu was put to death. Xieye then seized the whole of Zhala's estate.

sentences.zh: 大定間皆追正之。

translations.literal: Under Dading all these matters were posthumously rectified.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading era all these wrongs were posthumously set right.

sentences.zh: 海陵以兀魯有怨望語，斜也不奏，遂杖斜也，免所居官。

translations.literal: Because Wulu had spoken words of resentment and Xieye had not reported it, Hailing had Xieye beaten and removed him from his post.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wulu had uttered disloyal words and Xieye had failed to report them, Hailing had him beaten and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 俄，復為司徒，進拜太保，領三省事，兼勸農使。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made Minister of Education, advanced to Grand Guardian, oversaw the Three Departments, and concurrently served as Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored as Minister of Education, promoted to Grand Guardian, placed in charge of the Three Departments, and also named Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 再進太師，封梁晉國王。

translations.literal: He was further advanced to Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and Jin.

sentences.zh: 其妻先斜也卒，海陵嘗至其葬所致祭，起復其子率府率吾裏補為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His wife died before Xieye; Hailing once came to her burial place to offer sacrifice, and recalled his son Wulibu, Colonel of the Rate-Furnishing Office, from mourning to appoint him Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His wife predeceased him. Hailing once attended her funeral rites in person and recalled his son Wulibu, a colonel of the rate-furnishing office, from mourning to appoint him Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 大定間，海陵降為庶人，徒單氏為庶人妻，斜也降特進鞏國公。

translations.literal: Under Dading, Hailing was reduced to commoner status, Empress Tudan became a commoner's wife, and Xieye was demoted to Special Advancement Duke of Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading period Hailing was posthumously reduced to commoner rank, Empress Tudan to a commoner's wife, and Xieye demoted to Special Advancement Duke of Gong.

sentences.zh: 烏古論蒲魯虎

translations.literal: Wugulun Puluhu
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Puluhu

sentences.zh: 烏古論蒲魯虎，父當海，國初有功。

translations.literal: Wugulun Puluhu — his father Danghai had merit at the founding of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Puluhu was the son of Danghai, who had rendered distinguished service in the founding of the Jin state.

sentences.zh: 蒲魯虎通契丹大小字，娶宋王宗望女昭甯公主什古。

translations.literal: Puluhu mastered the large and small Khitan scripts; he married Princess Zhaoning Shigu, daughter of Prince Song Zongwang.
translations.idiomatic: Puluhu was fluent in both Khitan scripts and married Princess Zhaoning Shigu, daughter of Prince Song Zongwang.

sentences.zh: 熙宗初，為護衛，改牌印，常侍左右。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xizong's reign he was a guardsman, then changed to Keeper of Seals and attended constantly at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xizong's reign he served in the guard, then became Keeper of Seals and attended the emperor constantly.

sentences.zh: 轉通進。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Senior Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 襲父謀克，再遷臨海軍節度使，改衛州防禦使。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's meng'an command, was twice transferred to military governor of Linhai circuit, then changed to Defender of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's meng'an command, was twice promoted to military governor of Linhai, and then appointed Defender of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 海陵賜食內殿，謂之曰：「衛州風土甚佳，勿以防禦為降也。

translations.literal: Hailing granted him food in the inner palace and said to him: "Weizhou's climate and land are excellent — do not regard the post of Defender as a demotion."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing entertained him in the inner palace and said, "Weizhou enjoys excellent climate and soil — do not take the Defender's post as a demotion."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「頗聞衛州官署不利守者。

translations.literal: He replied: "I have often heard that the official residence at Weizhou is unlucky for those who hold it."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have often heard that Weizhou's official residence brings ill fortune to its occupants."

sentences.zh: 」即日改汾陽軍節度使，賜衣服、佩玉、帶劍。

translations.literal: That same day he was changed to military governor of Fenyang circuit and granted robes, girdle jade, and a sword.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he was transferred to military governor of Fenyang and bestowed robes, girdle jade, and a sword.

sentences.zh: 入為太子詹事，卒，年四十一。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died at forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died at forty-one.

sentences.zh: 海陵親臨哭之，后妃皆弔祭，賻贈甚厚。

translations.literal: Hailing came in person to mourn him; the empress and consorts all offered condolence sacrifices; funeral gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing came in person to mourn him; the empress and consorts all paid their respects; and the funeral gifts were lavish.

sentences.zh: 有司給喪事，贈特進駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: The relevant offices supplied funeral arrangements; posthumously enfeoffed as Special Advancement Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices arranged the funeral; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Special Advancement Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.

sentences.zh: 正隆例贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Under Zhenglong, by regulation he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenglong the standard posthumous rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness was conferred.

sentences.zh: 唐括德溫

translations.literal: Tangkuo Dewen
translations.idiomatic: Tangkuo Dewen

sentences.zh: 唐括德溫，本名阿里，上京率河人也。

translations.literal: Tangkuo Dewen — his original name was Ali; he was a man of Shuaihe in the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tangkuo Dewen, whose original name was Ali, came from Shuaihe in the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 曾祖石古，從太祖平臘醅麻產，領謀克。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shigu followed Taizu in pacifying Lapimai and held a meng'an command.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shigu followed Taizu in the pacification of Lapimai and held a meng'an command.

sentences.zh: 祖脫孛魯，領其父謀克，從太祖伐遼，攻甯江、泰州戰有功。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tuobolu inherited his father's meng'an command, followed Taizu in the campaign against Liao, and had merit in the battles at Ningjiang and Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tuobolu inherited the family meng'an command, campaigned with Taizu against Liao, and distinguished himself at Ningjiang and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 父撻懶，尚康宗女，從宋王宗望以軍二萬收平州，至城東十里許遇敵兵甚眾，戰敗之，太祖賞賚甚厚，授行軍猛安。

translations.literal: His father Talan married a daughter of Emperor Kangzong; he followed Prince Song Zongwang with twenty thousand troops to take Pingzhou. About ten li east of the city they encountered a very large enemy force, defeated them in battle, and Taizu rewarded him very generously, appointing him marching meng'an commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Talan married a daughter of Kangzong and followed Prince Song Zongwang with twenty thousand men to recover Pingzhou. Some ten li east of the city they met a large enemy host, routed it in battle, and Taizu rewarded him handsomely with appointment as marching meng'an commander.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，遷龍虎衛上將軍，歷興平、臨海等軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and successively served as military governor of Xingping, Linhai, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangtong he was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and served in turn as military governor of Xingping, Linhai, and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 十八年，追錄其父撻懶並德溫前後功，授其長子駙馬都尉鼎世襲西北路沒裏山猛安，徙隸泰州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the court posthumously recorded the merits of his father Talan and of Dewen's services before and after; his eldest son, Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household Dingshi, was granted hereditary succession to the Meilishan meng'an of the Northwestern Circuit and transferred to subordination under Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the court posthumously recorded Talan's merits together with Dewen's services. His eldest son Dingshi, Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household, was granted hereditary command of the Meilishan meng'an on the Northwestern Circuit and reassigned to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 烏古論粘沒曷

translations.literal: Wugulun Zhanmeihe
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Zhanmeihe

sentences.zh: 蒲察阿虎迭

translations.literal: Pucha Ahudie
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Ahudie

sentences.zh: 烏林答暉

translations.literal: Wulin Dahui
translations.idiomatic: Wulin Dahui

sentences.zh: 蒲察鼎壽

translations.literal: Pucha Dingshou
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Dingshou

sentences.zh: 蒲察鼎壽，本名和尚，上京曷速河人，欽懷皇后父也。

translations.literal: Pucha Dingshou — his original name was Heshang; he was a man of Yisuhe in the Upper Capital and was the father of Empress Qinhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Dingshou, whose original name was Heshang, came from Yisuhe in the Upper Capital and was the father of Empress Qinhuai.

sentences.zh: 賦性沉厚有明鑒，通契丹、漢字，長於吏事。

translations.literal: By nature he was steady and deep, with clear judgment; he mastered Khitan and Chinese scripts and excelled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Steady and perceptive by nature, he was fluent in Khitan and Chinese and excelled at government business.

sentences.zh: 尚熙宗女鄭國公主。

translations.literal: He married Princess Zheng of Zheng, a daughter of Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Zheng, a daughter of Xizong.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，以海陵女弟慶宜公主子加定遠大將軍，為尚衣局使，累官器物局使。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan 3, as son by marriage of Princess Qingyi, Hailing's younger sister, he was made General Who Pacifies the Far, Commissioner of the Wardrobe Bureau, and rose through posts to Commissioner of the Implements Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan, as son-in-law of Princess Qingyi, Hailing's younger sister, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Far, then Commissioner of the Wardrobe Bureau, and eventually Commissioner of the Implements Bureau.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，加駙馬都尉，職如故。

translations.literal: In Dading 2 he was additionally made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household; his duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he was also named Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household while retaining his existing duties.

sentences.zh: 曆符寶郎、蠡州刺史、浚州防禦使，有惠政，兩州百姓刻石紀之。

translations.literal: He successively served as Keeper of Seals, Prefect of Li, and Defender of Jun; his benevolent governance led the people of both prefectures to carve stone inscriptions commemorating him.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Keeper of Seals, Prefect of Li, and Defender of Jun, winning such goodwill that the people of both jurisdictions set up stone monuments in his honor.

sentences.zh: 遷泰甯軍節度使，歷東平府、橫海軍，入為右宣徽使，改左宣徽，授中都路昏得渾山猛安曷速木單世襲謀克。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Taining circuit, served at Dongping and Henghai, entered the capital as Right Commissioner of the Palace Attendants, was changed to the Left, and was granted hereditary succession to the Yisumu dan meng'an of Hundeshan in the Central Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became military governor of Taining, served at Dongping and on the Henghai frontier, entered court as Right then Left Commissioner of the Palace Attendants, and received hereditary command of the Yisumu dan meng'an at Hundeshan in the Central Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 改河間尹。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prefect of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Prefect of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 號令必行，豪右屏跡。

translations.literal: His orders were invariably enforced, and powerful local families kept out of sight.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were enforced without fail, and local magnates vanished from public view.

sentences.zh: 有宗室居河間，侵削居民，鼎壽奏徙其族于平州，郡內大治。

translations.literal: A member of the imperial clan residing in Hejian encroached on the populace; Dingshou memorialized to move the clan to Pingzhou, and within the commandery there was great order.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial clansman in Hejian preyed on local residents, Dingshou memorialized to relocate the clan to Pingzhou, and the prefecture was brought to good order.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 上聞之深加悼惜。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he deeply mourned and regretted the loss.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, on hearing the news, mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 喪至香山，皇太子往奠，百官致祭，賻銀彩絹。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached Xiangshan, the crown prince went to offer sacrifice; the hundred officials offered condolence rites; funeral gifts of silver and colored silks were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession reached Xiangshan, the crown prince came to offer sacrifice, officials paid their respects, and lavish gifts of silver and silk were sent.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，以皇后父贈太尉、越國公。

translations.literal: In Mingchang 3, as the empress's father he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Duke of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Mingchang he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Yue in his capacity as the empress's father.

sentences.zh: 鼎壽既世連姻戚，女為皇后，長子辭不失凡三尚定國、景國、道國公主。

translations.literal: Dingshou's family had for generations been connected by marriage with the throne; his daughter became empress, and his eldest son Cibushi had in all thrice married princesses of Ding, Jing, and Dao.
translations.idiomatic: The Dingshou family had long been tied to the throne by marriage; his daughter became empress, and his eldest son Cibushi married in turn the princesses of Ding, Jing, and Dao.

sentences.zh: 其寵遇如此，未嘗以富貴驕人，當時以為外戚之冠云。

translations.literal: Favored to this degree, he never grew arrogant on account of wealth and rank; contemporaries regarded him as the foremost among maternal kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Though favored to this degree, he never lorded his wealth and rank over others, and his contemporaries hailed him as the model among imperial affines.

sentences.zh: 徒單思忠

translations.literal: Tudan Sizhong
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Sizhong

sentences.zh: 徒單思忠，字良弼，本名甯慶。

translations.literal: Tudan Sizhong — courtesy name Liangbi, original name Ningqing.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Sizhong, courtesy name Liangbi, whose original name was Ningqing.

sentences.zh: 曾祖賽補，尚景祖女。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Saibu married a daughter of Emperor Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Saibu married a daughter of Jingzu.

sentences.zh: 從太祖伐遼，戰歿於臨潢之渾河。

translations.literal: He followed Taizu in the campaign against Liao and died in battle on the Hun River near Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizu against Liao and fell in battle on the Hun River near Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 父賽一，尚熙宗妹。

translations.literal: His father Saiyi married a younger sister of Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Saiyi married a younger sister of Xizong.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，為颭碗群牧使，契丹賊窩斡擾北邊，賽一與戰死之。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenglong he was Commissioner of the Zhanwan Horse Herds; the Khitan bandit Wowo disturbed the northern frontier, and Saiyi died fighting him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenglong he was Commissioner of the Zhanwan Horse Herds. When the Khitan rebel Wowo raided the northern frontier, Saiyi died fighting him.

sentences.zh: 大定初，贈金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he was posthumously made General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading he was posthumously appointed General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 十九年，上追念思忠輔立功，贈驃騎衛上將軍，乃授其子鐸武功將軍、世襲中都路烏獨渾謀克。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the emperor, recalling Sizhong's meritorious assistance, posthumously made him General-in-Chief of the Flying Cavalry Guard and granted his son Duo the rank of Martial Merit General with hereditary succession to the Wuduhun meng'an in the Central Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the emperor, recalling Sizhong's loyal service, posthumously appointed him General-in-Chief of the Flying Cavalry Guard and granted his son Duo the rank of Martial Merit General with hereditary command of the Wuduhun meng'an in the Central Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 徒單繹

translations.literal: Tudan Yi
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Yi

sentences.zh: 徒單繹，本名術輩，其先上京按出虎達阿人。

translations.literal: Tudan Yi — his original name was Shubei; his ancestors were men of Anchuhu Da'a in the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Yi, whose original name was Shubei, came from Anchuhu Da'a in the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 祖撒合懣，國初有功，授隆安府路合紮謀克、奪古阿鄰猛安。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sahemen had merit at the founding of the state and was appointed Hezha meng'an commander of Long'an prefecture circuit and meng'an of Duogu'alin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sahemen distinguished himself at the founding of the state and was appointed Hezha meng'an commander of Long'an circuit and meng'an of Duogu'alin.

sentences.zh: 繹美姿儀，通諸國語。

translations.literal: Yi was handsome in bearing and mastered the languages of the various states.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was striking in appearance and fluent in the languages of several peoples.

sentences.zh: 尚熙宗第七女沈國公主。

translations.literal: He married Princess Shen of Shen, the seventh daughter of Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Shen, Xizong's seventh daughter.

sentences.zh: 充符寶祗候，遷御院通進，授符寶郎。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Keeper of Seals, was transferred to Senior Remonstrator of the Imperial Household, and appointed Keeper of Seals.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant Keeper of Seals, was promoted to Senior Remonstrator of the Imperial Household, and appointed Keeper of Seals.

sentences.zh: 曆宣德、泰安、淄州刺史，有廉名。

translations.literal: He successively served as Prefect of Xuande, Tai'an, and Zi and gained a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Xuande, Tai'an, and Zi and earned a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 改同知廣寧府事，以母鄂國公主憂，不赴。

translations.literal: He was changed to Associate Administrator of Guangning prefecture but, on account of mourning for his mother Princess E of E, did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Associate Administrator of Guangning but declined the post while in mourning for his mother, Princess E.

sentences.zh: 世宗特許以憂制中襲父封。

translations.literal: Shizong specially permitted him to inherit his father's enfeoffment while still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong specially allowed him to inherit his father's title while still in mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闕，授同知濟南府事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Associate Administrator of Jinan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was appointed Associate Administrator of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，遷棣州防禦使，以政跡聞，升臨海軍節度使，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to Defender of Di, became known for his administrative record, was promoted to military governor of Linhai circuit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenty-sixth year of service he became Defender of Di, won notice for his governance, was promoted to military governor of Linhai, and died.

sentences.zh: 繹家世貴寵，自會祖照至繹尚公主者凡四世云。

translations.literal: Yi's family had for generations enjoyed noble favor; from his great-grandfather Zhao down to Yi, those who married princesses numbered four generations in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi family had long enjoyed imperial favor: from his great-grandfather Zhao down to Yi himself, four generations in succession had married imperial princesses.

sentences.zh: 烏林答復

translations.literal: Wulin Dafu
translations.idiomatic: Wulin Dafu

sentences.zh: 烏林答復，本名阿裏剌，東平人也。

translations.literal: Wulin Dafu — his original name was Alila; he was a man of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Wulin Dafu, whose original name was Alila, was a native of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 奉御出身，大定七年尚世宗第七女宛國公主，授駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Rising from palace attendant, in Dading 7 he married Princess Wan of Wan, the seventh daughter of Shizong, and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.
translations.idiomatic: A former palace attendant, he married Princess Wan, Shizong's seventh daughter, in the seventh year of Dading and was named Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.

sentences.zh: 改引進使、兼符寶郎，出為蠡州刺史，三遷歸德軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Commissioner of Introduction and concurrent Keeper of Seals, went out as Prefect of Li, and after three promotions became military governor of Guide circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became Commissioner of Introduction and concurrent Keeper of Seals, served as Prefect of Li, and after three promotions became military governor of Guide.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，轉知興中府事，久之，為曷懶路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In Mingchang 3 he was transferred to Administrator of Xingzhong prefecture; after a long interval he became Supreme Commander of the Yilan circuit forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Mingchang he was made Administrator of Xingzhong; long afterward he became supreme commander of the Yilan circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，拜絳陽軍節度使。

translations.literal: In Cheng'an 4 he was appointed military governor of Jiangyang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was appointed military governor of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 烏古論元忠

translations.literal: Wugulun Yuanzhong
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Yuanzhong

sentences.zh: 會大興府守臣闕，遂以元忠知府事。

translations.literal: When the post of defender of Daxing prefecture was vacant, Yuanzhong was accordingly appointed to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of prefect of Daxing fell vacant, Yuanzhong was appointed to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有僧犯法，吏甫得置獄，皇姑梁國大長公主屬使釋之，元忠不聽，主奏其事，世宗召謂曰：「卿不徇情，甚可嘉也，治京如此，朕復何憂。

translations.literal: A monk violated the law and the clerks had just placed him in prison when the emperor's paternal aunt, the Grand Princess of Liang, sent orders to release him; Yuanzhong would not comply. The princess reported the matter, and Shizong summoned him and said: "You do not yield to private feeling — this is highly commendable. If the capital is governed thus, what have I to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: When a monk broke the law and officials had just imprisoned him, the emperor's paternal aunt, the Grand Princess of Liang, ordered his release. Yuanzhong refused. After she reported him, Shizong summoned him and said, "You do not bend to private influence — that is admirable. If the capital is governed this way, what have I to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」秩滿，授吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以其子誼尚顯宗長女薛國公主。

translations.literal: His son Yi married Princess Xue of Xue, the eldest daughter of Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi married Princess Xue, the eldest daughter of Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢御史大夫，授撒巴山世襲謀克。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and granted hereditary succession to the Sabashan meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and granted hereditary command of the Sabashan meng'an.

sentences.zh: 世宗問左丞相紇石烈良弼孰可相者，良弼以元忠對，乃拜平章政事，封任國公，進尚書右丞相。

translations.literal: Shizong asked the Left Chief Councillor Hesheli Liangbi who could serve as chief minister; Liangbi named Yuanzhong, and he was thereupon appointed Grand Councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Ren, and advanced to Right Chief Councillor of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong asked Left Chief Councillor Hesheli Liangbi whom he might appoint chief minister, Liangbi recommended Yuanzhong. Yuanzhong was made Grand Councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Ren, and promoted to Right Chief Councillor.

sentences.zh: 策論進士之科設，元忠贊成之。

translations.literal: When the examination category for Policy Essay Jinshi was established, Yuanzhong supported it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Policy Essay jinshi examination was instituted, Yuanzhong endorsed it.

sentences.zh: 世宗將幸會寧，元忠進諫不聽，出知真定府，尋復詔為右丞相。

translations.literal: When Shizong was about to visit Huining, Yuanzhong remonstrated but was not heeded; he was sent out to administer Zhending prefecture, then soon recalled by edict as Right Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong planned a visit to Huining, Yuanzhong remonstrated in vain and was posted to Zhending, but was soon recalled as Right Chief Councillor.

sentences.zh: 世宗欲甓上京城，元忠曰：「此邦遭正隆軍興，百姓凋弊，陛下休養二十餘年，尚未完復。

translations.literal: Shizong wished to pave the Upper Capital with brick; Yuanzhong said: "This region suffered the military campaigns of Zhenglong; the people are depleted. Your Majesty has rested and nurtured them for more than twenty years, yet recovery is still incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong proposed paving the Upper Capital with brick, Yuanzhong said, "This region was ravaged by Zhenglong's wars and the people remain exhausted. Your Majesty has given them more than twenty years to recover, yet restoration is still incomplete.

sentences.zh: 況土性疏惡，甓之恐難經久，風雨摧壞，歲歲繕完，民將益因矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the soil is loose and poor; brick paving would probably not last, and when wind and rain destroyed it, yearly repairs would only burden the people further."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the soil is loose and poor; brick paving would likely not endure, and when wind and rain wore it away yearly repairs would only burden the people further."

sentences.zh: 」駕東幸久之未還，元忠奏曰：「鸞輿駐此已閱歲，倉儲日少，市買漸貴，禁衛暨諸局署多逃者，有司捕置諸法恐傷陛下仁愛。

translations.literal: The imperial progress eastward had long failed to return; Yuanzhong memorialized: "The imperial carriage has remained here for a full year; storehouses dwindle daily and market prices rise; many of the guard and the various bureaus have fled. If the authorities arrest and punish them by law, I fear it will wound Your Majesty's benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: The eastern tour had long delayed the emperor's return. Yuanzhong memorialized, "The imperial carriage has lingered here a full year; stores dwindle daily and prices rise; many guards and bureau staff have fled. If officials arrest and punish them by the full rigor of law, Your Majesty's reputation for mercy may suffer."

sentences.zh: 」世宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Shizong praised and accepted the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong commended and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 尋出為北京留守，責諭之曰：「汝強悍自用，顓權而結近密。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as military governor of the Northern Capital; he was rebuked and instructed: "You are overbearing and self-willed, monopolize power, and cultivate intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posted as military governor of the Northern Capital and rebuked: "You are overbearing and self-willed, monopolize power, and cultivate a private circle.

sentences.zh: 汝心叵測，其速之官。

translations.literal: Your intentions are hard to fathom — go quickly to your post."
translations.idiomatic: Your intentions are hard to read — go to your post at once."

sentences.zh: 」後左丞張汝弼奏事，世宗惡其阿順，謂左右曰：「卿等每事依違苟避，不肯盡言，高爵厚祿何以勝任。

translations.literal: Later, when Left Vice Councillor Zhang Rubi presented affairs, Shizong disliked his flattery and said to those beside him: "You all hedge and evade on every matter and will not speak fully — with high rank and rich salary, how can you be equal to your duties?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Left Vice Councillor Zhang Rubi reported on affairs, Shizong disliked his flattery and told his attendants, "You hedge and dodge on every issue and will not speak plainly — with high rank and rich salary, how can you be fit for office?

sentences.zh: 如烏古論元忠為相，剛直敢言，義不顧身，誠可尚也。

translations.literal: One like Wugulun Yuanzhong as chief minister — upright, daring to speak, righteous without regard for his person — is truly to be honored."
translations.idiomatic: A man like Wugulun Yuanzhong as chief minister — upright, outspoken, righteous without regard for himself — is truly admirable."

sentences.zh: 」於是，改知真定府事，移知河間。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was changed to Administrator of Zhending prefecture and transferred to administer Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was then reassigned to administer Zhending and later Hejian.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，知廣寧府。

translations.literal: In Mingchang 2 he administered Guangning prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingchang he governed Guangning.

sentences.zh: 以河間修築球場擾民，會赦下，除順義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Because at Hejian he had built a ball court that disturbed the people, when an amnesty was issued he was made military governor of Shunyi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After building a ball court at Hejian that harassed the populace, he was appointed military governor of Shunyi when an amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕不許，特加開府儀同三司、北京留守。

translations.literal: He requested retirement but was not permitted; he was specially advanced to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Pouch and made military governor of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire but was refused; he was specially promoted to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Pouch and reappointed military governor of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 徙知濟南府，過闕，令預宴，班平章政事之上。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Jinan prefecture; passing the palace, he was ordered to attend banquets and ranked above the grand councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Jinan, he was summoned to court banquets and seated above the grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，移守南京，尋改知彰德府，卒。

translations.literal: In Cheng'an 2 he was transferred to guard Nanjing; soon after he was changed to Administrator of Zhangde prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Cheng'an he was transferred to Nanjing, soon afterward made Administrator of Zhangde, and died.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，上遣宣徽使白琬燒飯，賻物甚厚。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, the emperor sent Commissioner of the Palace Attendants Bai Wan to offer funeral food; condolence gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: On news of his death the emperor sent Palace Attendant Commissioner Bai Wan to offer funeral sacrifices, with lavish condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 元忠素貴，性粗豪而內深忌，世宗嘗責之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong had long been noble; by nature he was rough and bold yet inwardly deeply jealous, and Shizong once rebuked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong had long enjoyed high standing; outwardly bold and rough, inwardly jealous, and Shizong once reproved him for it.

sentences.zh: 又所至不能戢奴僕，世以此為訾云。

translations.literal: Moreover, wherever he went he could not restrain his household slaves; the age criticized him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Nor could he restrain his household slaves wherever he served, for which contemporaries criticized him.

sentences.zh: 子誼。

translations.literal: His son Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi.

sentences.zh: 誼本名雄名。

translations.literal: Yi's original name was Xiongming.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, whose original name was Xiongming.

sentences.zh: 大定八年，尚海陵女。

translations.literal: In Dading 8 he married a daughter of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dading he married a daughter of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 宴宗室及六品以上官，命婦預焉，上曰：「此女亦太祖之曾孫，猶朕之女，乃父廢亡，非其女之罪也。

translations.literal: He feasted the imperial clan and officials of the sixth rank and above; titled ladies also attended. The emperor said: "This woman too is a great-granddaughter of Taizu, no different from my own daughter; her father was deposed and destroyed — it is not her fault."
translations.idiomatic: At a feast for the imperial clan and officials of the sixth rank and above, with titled ladies present, the emperor said, "She too is Taizu's great-granddaughter, no different from my own daughter. Her father was deposed and destroyed — the fault is not hers."

sentences.zh: 」海陵女卒，大定二十一年，尚顯宗女廣平郡主。

translations.literal: When Hailing's daughter died, in Dading 21 he married the Princess of Guangping, a daughter of Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing's daughter died, he married the Princess of Guangping, a daughter of Xianzong, in the twenty-first year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 誼歷仕宮衛，為人粗豪類其父。

translations.literal: Yi served successively in the palace guard; in character he was rough and bold like his father.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served in the palace guard and, like his father, was rough and overbearing in manner.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，上謂原王曰：「元忠勿望其可復相也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor said to Prince Yuan: "Do not expect that Yuanzhong can again become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor told Prince Yuan, "Do not imagine Yuanzhong can become chief minister again.

sentences.zh: 雄名又不及乃父，朕嘗宥待，殊不知恩，汝宜知其為人。

translations.literal: Xiongming is even less capable than his father; I once treated him with forbearance, yet he knows nothing of gratitude — you should understand what sort of man he is."
translations.idiomatic: Xiongming falls even shorter of his father. I once treated him leniently, yet he shows no gratitude. You should know what manner of man he is."

sentences.zh: 」謂平章政事襄曰：「雄名可令補外。

translations.literal: He said to Grand Councilor Xiang: "Xiongming may be sent to fill an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: He told Grand Councilor Xiang, "Xiongming should be posted outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 自今宮掖官已有旨補外者，比及廷授，即毋令入宮。

translations.literal: From now on, whenever a palace official has already received orders to fill an outside post, once court appointment is imminent he must not be allowed to enter the palace."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whenever a palace official has been ordered to an outside post, he must not enter the palace again once court appointment is imminent."

sentences.zh: 」於是，誼除同知澄州軍州事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi was appointed Associate Administrator of Chengzhou army-and-prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was then appointed Associate Administrator of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，廣平郡主進封鄴國長公主，誼改順天軍節度副使，加駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, the Princess of Guangping was advanced to Grand Princess of Ye; Yi was changed to Vice Military Governor of Shuntian circuit and additionally made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong came to the throne, the Princess of Guangping was promoted to Grand Princess of Ye. Yi became Vice Military Governor of Shuntian and was also named Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.

sentences.zh: 承安元年，累遷秘書監兼吏部侍郎，改刑部，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In Cheng'an 1 he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Palace Library and concurrent Vice Minister of Personnel, was changed to the Ministry of Punishments, and was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Cheng'an he rose to Director of the Palace Library and concurrent Vice Minister of Personnel, then served in the Ministry of Punishments and was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，遇父元忠憂。

translations.literal: In Taihe 1 he entered mourning for his father Yuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taihe he went into mourning for his father Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 二年，以本官起復。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled from mourning to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled from mourning to his former post.

sentences.zh: 三年，知東平府事，改知真定府事。

translations.literal: In the third year he administered Dongping prefecture and was changed to administer Zhending prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he governed Dongping, then was transferred to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 六年，伐宋，遷元帥左都監。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, during the campaign against Song, he was transferred to Left Supervisor of the Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, in the campaign against Song, he was made Left Supervisor of the Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉左監軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Left Army Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Left Army Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 八年，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 大安中，知大名府。

translations.literal: During Da'an he administered Daming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Da'an he governed Daming.

sentences.zh: 至甯初，以謀逆伏誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhining he was executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhining he was executed for treason.

sentences.zh: 唐括貢

translations.literal: Tangkuo Gong
translations.idiomatic: Tangkuo Gong

sentences.zh: 唐括貢，本名達哥，太傅阿裏之子也。

translations.literal: Tangkuo Gong — his original name was Dage; he was the son of Grand Preceptor Ali.
translations.idiomatic: Tangkuo Gong, whose original name was Dage, was the son of Grand Preceptor Ali.

sentences.zh: 尚世宗第四女吳國公主，授駙馬都尉，充奉御。

translations.literal: He married Princess Wu of Wu, the fourth daughter of Shizong; he was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household and served as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Wu, Shizong's fourth daughter, was named Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household, and served as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 特授拱衛直副都指揮使，五遷刑部侍郎，坐擅離職削官一階，出為德州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Deputy Commander of the Arch-Guard Direct Command; after five promotions he became Vice Minister of Punishments; for leaving his post without authorization one rank was stripped and he went out as Defender of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially made Deputy Commander of the Arch-Guard Direct Command, rose through five promotions to Vice Minister of Punishments, lost one rank for unauthorized absence from office, and was posted as Defender of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 升順天軍節度使，移鎮橫海。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military governor of Shuntian circuit and transferred to command Henghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military governor of Shuntian and transferred to Henghai.

sentences.zh: 召為左宣徽使，遷兵部尚書，改吏部，轉禮部尚書、兼大理卿。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Left Commissioner of the Palace Attendants, transferred to Minister of War, changed to Minister of Personnel, and transferred to Minister of Rites with concurrent service as Chief Judge of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Left Commissioner of the Palace Attendants, he became Minister of War, then Minister of Personnel, and finally Minister of Rites while also serving as Chief Judge of the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 先是，大理卿闕，世宗命宰臣選可授者，左丞張汝弼舉西京副留守楊子益法律詳明。

translations.literal: Earlier the post of Chief Judge of the Court of Review had been vacant; Shizong ordered the chief ministers to select someone fit for appointment. Left Vice Councillor Zhang Rubi recommended Yang Ziyi, Deputy Military Governor of the Western Capital, as expert in law.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief judgeship of the Court of Review fell vacant, Shizong ordered the chief ministers to choose a candidate. Left Vice Councillor Zhang Rubi recommended Yang Ziyi, Deputy Military Governor of the Western Capital, as expert in law.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「子益雖明法，而用心不正，豈可任之以分別天下是非也？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Though Ziyi understands law, his intentions are not upright — how can he be entrusted to distinguish right and wrong throughout the realm?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ziyi may know the law, but his heart is not upright. How can he be entrusted to judge right and wrong for the whole realm?

sentences.zh: 大理須用公正人。

translations.literal: The Court of Review must employ a man of fairness."
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Review requires a man of integrity."

sentences.zh: 」左丞粘割斡特剌舉貢可任以閑簡部分而兼領是職，遂以貢為之。

translations.literal: Left Vice Councillor Zhagu Watela recommended that Gong was capable and, given his leisure from other duties, could concurrently hold this office; Gong was accordingly appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Councillor Zhagu Watela argued that Gong was capable and, given his lighter duties, could hold the post concurrently, and Gong was appointed.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 章宗立，為御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, he became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong came to the throne, he was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 會貢生日，右丞相襄、參知政事劉瑋、吏部郎中肼、中都兵馬都指揮使和喜為貢壽，遂犯夜禁，和喜遣軍人送襄至第。

translations.literal: It happened to be Gong's birthday; Right Chief Councillor Xiang, Participating Councillor Liu Wei, Director of the Personnel Bureau Bing, and Supreme Commander of the Central Capital forces Hexi came to congratulate Gong and thereby violated the night curfew; Hexi sent soldiers to escort Xiang to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: On Gong's birthday, Right Chief Councillor Xiang, Participating Councillor Liu Wei, Director of the Personnel Bureau Bing, and Central Capital supreme commander Hexi came to celebrate and violated the night curfew. Hexi sent soldiers to escort Xiang home.

sentences.zh: 監察御史徒單德勝劾其事，下刑部逮肼等問狀。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Tudan Desheng impeached the matter; the Ministry of Punishments was ordered to arrest Bing and the others and examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Tudan Desheng impeached them, and the Ministry of Punishments was ordered to arrest Bing and the others for questioning.

sentences.zh: 上以襄、瑋大臣釋之，而貢等各解職。

translations.literal: The emperor released Xiang and Wei as great ministers, but Gong and the others each resigned their offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released Xiang and Wei as senior ministers, while Gong and the others resigned their posts.

sentences.zh: 尋知大興府事，復為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Before long he administered Daxing prefecture and was again made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he governed Daxing and was restored as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕不許，進樞密使，封莘國公，改封蕭。

translations.literal: He requested retirement but was not permitted; he was advanced to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Shen, then changed to Duke of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: His request to retire was refused; he was promoted to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Shen, and later as Duke of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 復上表乞退，上曰：「向已嘗告，續知意欲外除，今之告將復若何。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial requesting withdrawal; the emperor said: "You have already petitioned once; I further know you wish to be posted outside the capital — what will this new petition mean?"
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned again to retire. The emperor said, "You have already asked once, and I know you want an outside post. What do you expect from this new request?"

sentences.zh: 」遂優詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict of special favor thereupon permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict then granted his request.

sentences.zh: 尋起知真定府事。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to administer Zhending prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to govern Zhending.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年，薨。

translations.literal: In Taihe 2 he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 烏林答琳

translations.literal: Wulin Dalin
translations.idiomatic: Wulin Dalin

sentences.zh: 烏林答琳，本名留住。

translations.literal: Wulin Dalin — his original name was Liuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Wulin Dalin, whose original name was Liuzhu.

sentences.zh: 尚郜國公主，加駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Princess Gao of Gao and was additionally made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Gao and was named Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年為靜難軍節度使。

translations.literal: In Zhenyou 1 he was military governor of Jingnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyou he was military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 夏人犯邠州，琳降。

translations.literal: When the Xia attacked Binzhou, Lin surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Xia attacked Binzhou, Lin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 會延安府遣通事張福孫至夏國，夏人使福孫見琳，時已中風，公主令人以狀付福孫，屬以懇禱朝廷，冀早太平得還鄉之意。

translations.literal: It happened that Yan'an prefecture sent interpreter Zhang Fusun to the Xia state; the Xia had Fusun see Lin, who by then had suffered a stroke. The princess had someone give Fusun a written account, entrusting him to plead earnestly with the court, hoping for early peace and a return home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan'an sent interpreter Zhang Fusun to Western Xia, the Xia arranged for him to see Lin, who had already suffered a stroke. The princess gave Fusun a written account asking him to plead with the court for peace so they might return home.

sentences.zh: 福孫具以聞，詔賜以藥物。

translations.literal: Fusun reported everything in full; an edict bestowed medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Fusun reported the full account, and an edict sent medicines as a gift.

sentences.zh: 徒單公弼

translations.literal: Tudan Gongbi
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Gongbi

sentences.zh: 徒單公弼，本名習烈，河北東路算主海猛安人。

translations.literal: Tudan Gongbi — his original name was Xilie; he was a man of the Suanzhuhai meng'an on the Hebei Eastern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Gongbi, whose original name was Xilie, came from the Suanzhuhai meng'an on the Hebei Eastern Circuit.

sentences.zh: 父府君奴，尚熙宗女，加駙馬都尉，終武定軍節度使。

translations.literal: His father Fujunnu married a daughter of Xizong, was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household, and ended as military governor of Wuding circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fujunnu married a daughter of Xizong, became Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household, and ended his career as military governor of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 公弼初充奉御，大定二十七年，尚世宗女息國公主，加定遠大將軍、駙馬都尉，改器物局直長。

translations.literal: Gongbi first served as palace attendant; in Dading 27 he married Princess Xi of Xi, a daughter of Shizong, was made General Who Pacifies the Far and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household, and was changed to Director of the Implements Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi began as a palace attendant. In the twenty-seventh year of Dading he married Princess Xi, Shizong's daughter, was named General Who Pacifies the Far and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household, and became Director of the Implements Bureau.

sentences.zh: 轉副使、兼近侍局直長。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Deputy Commissioner and concurrent Director of the Inner Attendants Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He became Deputy Commissioner and concurrent Director of the Inner Attendants Bureau.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起復本局副使。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he entered mourning, then was recalled from mourning to his former post as deputy commissioner of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he mourned, then was recalled to his former deputy commissionership.

sentences.zh: 章宗秋山射中虎，虎怒突而前，侍衛皆避去，公弼不動，虎亦隨斃。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong shot a tiger on the autumn hunt, the tiger in rage charged forward; the guards all fled, but Gongbi did not move, and the tiger was soon killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong shot a tiger on the autumn hunt, the wounded beast charged. The guards scattered, but Gongbi stood his ground, and the tiger was soon killed.

sentences.zh: 詔責侍衛而慰諭公弼。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked the guards and comforted Gongbi with praise.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked the guards and commended Gongbi.

sentences.zh: 除濱州刺史，再遷兵部侍郎，累除知大名府事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Bin, twice transferred to Vice Minister of War, and repeatedly appointed to administer Daming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Prefect of Bin, promoted twice to Vice Minister of War, and served repeatedly as administrator of Daming.

sentences.zh: 是時，伐宋軍興，有司督逋租及牛頭稅甚急，公弼奏：「軍士從戎，民亦疲弊，可緩徵以紓民。

translations.literal: At that time war against Song had begun; the authorities pressed collection of overdue rents and the ox-head tax very urgently. Gongbi memorialized: "Soldiers follow the army to war, and the people are also exhausted — collection may be slowed to relieve the populace."
translations.idiomatic: War against Song had begun, and officials pressed hard for overdue rents and the ox-head tax. Gongbi memorialized, "Soldiers are at war and the people are exhausted. Collection should be eased to give them relief."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 大安初，知大興府事，讞武清盜，疑其有冤，已而果獲真盜。

translations.literal: Early in Da'an he administered Daxing prefecture; in a theft case at Wuqing he doubted there had been a miscarriage of justice, and afterward the real thief was indeed captured.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Da'an he governed Daxing. In a theft case at Wuqing he suspected a wrongful conviction, and the real thief was later captured.

sentences.zh: 歲餘拜參知政事，進右丞，轉左丞。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Participating Councillor, advanced to Right Vice Councillor, and transferred to Left Vice Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was made Participating Councillor, promoted to Right Vice Councillor, then Left Vice Councillor.

sentences.zh: 至甯初，拜平章政事，封定國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhining he was appointed Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhining he was made Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ding.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，進拜右丞相，罷知中山府事。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyou he was advanced to Right Chief Councillor and relieved of administering Zhongshan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou he was promoted to Right Chief Councillor and relieved of his post at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 是時，中都圍急不可行，圍解，宣宗曰：「中山新被兵，不如河中善。

translations.literal: At that time the Central Capital was under tight siege and travel was impossible; when the siege was lifted, Xuanzong said: "Zhongshan has newly suffered warfare — Hezhong would be better."
translations.idiomatic: The Central Capital was then under siege and impassable. When the siege lifted, Xuanzong said, "Zhongshan has just been ravaged by war. Hezhong would be safer."

sentences.zh: 」乃改知河中府。

translations.literal: He was accordingly changed to Administrator of Hezhong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to govern Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 曆定國軍節度使事、太孫太師、同判大睦親府事。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of military governor of Dingguo circuit, Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, and Associate Judge of the Great Bureau of Imperial Kinship.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as military governor of Dingguo, Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, and Associate Judge of the Great Bureau of Imperial Kinship.

sentences.zh: 興定五年薨，宣宗輟朝，賻贈，諡恪願。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xingding he died; Xuanzong suspended court, bestowed funeral gifts, and gave the posthumous title Ke-Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Xingding. Xuanzong suspended court, sent lavish funeral gifts, and posthumously titled him Ke-Yuan.

sentences.zh: 徒單銘

translations.literal: Tudan Ming
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Ming

sentences.zh: 贊曰：天子娶后，王姬下嫁，豈不重哉。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When the Son of Heaven takes a queen and royal daughters marry down, is this not weighty indeed?
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: When the Son of Heaven takes a queen and royal daughters marry downward in rank, how weighty a matter that is.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以來，無世世甥舅之家。

translations.literal: Since Qin and Han there have been no families of maternal uncles and nephews generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin and Han there had been no dynasty in which the same maternal clans served as affines generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 《關雎》之道缺，外戚驕盈，《何彼穠矣》不作，王姬肅雝之義幾希矣。

translations.literal: The way of the "Ospreys" was lacking, maternal kinsmen grew arrogant and full; the "How Luxuriant" was no longer composed, and the solemn dignity owed to royal daughters was nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of the "Ospreys" was lost, maternal kinsmen grew arrogant, the "How Luxuriant" was no longer heard, and the solemn dignity owed to royal daughters had nearly vanished.

sentences.zh: 蓋古者異姓世爵公侯與天子為昏因，他姓不得參焉。

translations.literal: For in antiquity only enfeoffed lords of other surnames who held hereditary noble rank formed marriage alliances with the Son of Heaven; other clans could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity only hereditary noble houses of other surnames formed marriage alliances with the throne; no other clans could enter that circle.

sentences.zh: 女為王后，己尚王姬，而自貴其貴，富厚不加焉，寵榮不與焉。

translations.literal: When a daughter became queen, one had already married a royal daughter; thus one valued one's own nobility, without adding further wealth, and without sharing in favor and glory.
translations.idiomatic: When a daughter became empress, one had already married a royal princess; the clan rested on its own nobility without piling on further wealth or sharing in imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 使漢、唐行此道，則無呂氏、王氏、武氏之難，公主下嫁各安其分、各得其所矣。

translations.literal: Had Han and Tang followed this way, there would have been no disasters of the Lü, Wang, and Wu clans, and princesses marrying down would each have kept their proper place and found their proper station.
translations.idiomatic: Had Han and Tang followed this practice, there would have been no catastrophes of the Lü, Wang, and Wu clans, and princesses marrying down would each have kept their proper place.

sentences.zh: 金之徒單、拿懶、唐括、蒲察、裴滿、紇石烈、僕散皆貴族也，天子娶後必於是，公主下嫁必於是，與周之齊、紀無異，此昏禮之最得宜者，盛于漢、唐矣。

translations.literal: The Tudan, Nalan, Tangkuo, Pucha, Peiman, Hesheli, and Pusan clans of Jin were all noble houses; the Son of Heaven taking a queen and princesses marrying down had to be from among them — no different from the Qi and Ji of Zhou. This was the most fitting marriage institution, surpassing Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Tudan, Nalan, Tangkuo, Pucha, Peiman, Hesheli, and Pusan were all noble clans. Emperors took empresses only from them, and princesses married only among them — no different from Zhou's Qi and Ji. This was the soundest marriage practice, surpassing even Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 徒單四喜

translations.literal: Tudan Sixi
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Sixi

sentences.zh: 徒單四喜，哀宗皇后之弟也。

translations.literal: Tudan Sixi was the younger brother of Aizong's empress.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Sixi was the younger brother of Empress Tudan, consort of Aizong.

sentences.zh: 天興二年正月辛酉夜，四喜、內侍馬福惠至自歸德，時河朔已失利，京城猶未知，二人被旨迎兩宮，遂託以報捷，執小黃旗以入，至則奏兩宮以奉迎之意。

translations.literal: On the night of xinyou in the first month of Tianxing 2, Sixi and palace attendant Ma Fuhui arrived from Guide. The Hebei north had already suffered defeat, but the capital still did not know. The two had been ordered to welcome the two palaces; they therefore pretended to bring news of victory, entered holding small yellow banners, and upon arrival reported to the two palaces the intention to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou night of the first month of Tianxing 2, Sixi and palace attendant Ma Fuhui arrived from Guide. The north had already been lost, though the capital did not yet know it. Ordered to welcome the two palaces, they pretended to bring news of victory, entered with small yellow banners, and reported the plan to escort the empress dowagers.

sentences.zh: 是日，召二相入議，二相及烏古孫奴申諫不可行。

translations.literal: That day the two chief ministers were summoned to deliberate; the two chief ministers and Wugusun Nushen remonstrated that the plan could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: That day the two chief ministers were summoned to council. They and Wugusun Nushen urged that the move could not be made.

sentences.zh: 四喜作色曰：「我奉制旨迎兩宮，有敢言不行者，當以別敕從事矣。

translations.literal: Sixi changed color and said: "I carry an imperial order to welcome the two palaces — whoever dares say it cannot be done will be dealt with by separate edict."
translations.idiomatic: Sixi flushed and said, "I carry an imperial order to welcome the two palaces. Anyone who says it cannot be done will be punished by separate edict."

sentences.zh: 」二相不復敢言，行議遂決。

translations.literal: The two chief ministers no longer dared speak, and the plan to depart was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The two chief ministers fell silent, and the departure was decided.
