sentences.zh: 制旨所取兩宮、柔妃裴滿氏及令人張秀蕊、都轄、承御、湯藥、皇乳母鞏國夫人等十餘人外，皆放遣之。

translations.literal: Apart from the two palaces, Gentle Consort Peiman, Lady-in-Waiting Zhang Xiurui, directors, attendants, medicine officers, the imperial wet nurse Lady of Gong, and more than ten others specified in the order, all others were dismissed and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the two palaces, Gentle Consort Peiman, Lady-in-Waiting Zhang Xiurui, directors, attendants, medicine officers, the imperial wet nurse Lady of Gong, and a dozen others named in the order, everyone else was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又取宮中寶物，馬蹄金四百杖、大珠如栗黃者七千杖、生金山一、龍腦板二及信瑞御璽，仍許賜忠孝軍以兩宮隨行物之半。

translations.literal: Palace treasures were also taken: four hundred ingots of horse-hoof gold, seven thousand large chestnut-yellow pearls, one raw-gold mountain, two boards of borneol, and the imperial seals of trust and auspice; it was further permitted to grant the Loyal and Filial Army half of the two palaces' traveling goods.
translations.idiomatic: Palace treasures were also taken: four hundred ingots of horse-hoof gold, seven thousand large chestnut-yellow pearls, one raw-gold mountain, two boards of borneol, and the imperial seals of trust and auspice. Half of the two palaces' traveling goods were granted to the Loyal and Filial Army.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，太后御仁安殿，出錠金及七寶金洗分賜忠孝軍。

translations.literal: On renyin the empress dowager presided at Rén'an Hall, brought out ingot gold and seven-jewel gold basins, and distributed them to the Loyal and Filial Army.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the empress dowager appeared at Ren'an Hall, distributed ingot gold and seven-jewel gold basins among the Loyal and Filial Army.

sentences.zh: 是夜，兩宮騎而出，至陳留，見城外二三處火起，疑有兵，遲回間，奴申初不欲行，即承太后旨馳還。

translations.literal: That night the two palaces rode out; reaching Chenliu they saw two or three fires rise outside the walls and suspected troops; while hesitating, Nushen, who from the first had not wished to go, received the empress dowager's order and galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: That night the two palaces rode out. At Chenliu they saw fires outside the walls and suspected enemy troops. While they hesitated, Nushen—who had opposed the move from the start—received the empress dowager's order and galloped back.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，入京頓四喜家，少頃，還宮。

translations.literal: On guimao they entered the capital and lodged at Sixi's house; after a short while they returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao they entered the capital and stayed briefly at Sixi's house before returning to the palace.

sentences.zh: 復議以是夜再往，太后憊于鞍馬不能動，遂止。

translations.literal: They again deliberated going out that same night, but the empress dowager was exhausted from riding and could not move, so the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They debated setting out again that night, but the empress dowager was too exhausted from riding to continue, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 明日，崔立變。

translations.literal: The next day Cui Li mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Cui Li staged his mutiny.

sentences.zh: 四喜、術甲塔失不及塔失不之父咬住、四喜妻完顏氏，以忠孝卒九十七騎奪曹門而出，將往歸德，不得出，轉陳州門，亦為門卒所止。

translations.literal: Sixi, Shujia Tashi, Tashi's father Yaozhu, and Sixi's wife of the Wanyan clan, with ninety-seven horsemen of the Loyal and Filial Army, seized the Cao Gate and broke out, intending to go to Guide but unable to get out; they turned to the Chenzhou Gate and were also stopped by gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: Sixi, Shujia Tashi, Tashi's father Yaozhu, Sixi's Wanyan wife, and ninety-seven Loyal and Filial horsemen forced the Cao Gate and tried to reach Guide but could not get out. They turned to the Chenzhou Gate and were stopped there as well.

sentences.zh: 門帥裕州防禦使阿不罕斜合已遁去，經歷官完顏合住權帥職，麾門卒放塔失不等去，且曰：「罪在我，非汝等之過。

translations.literal: The gate commander, Defender of Yuzhou Abuhan Xiehe, had already fled; the administrative officer Wanyan Hezhu assumed command pro tempore, ordered the gate guards to release Tashi and the others, and said: "The guilt is mine, not yours."
translations.idiomatic: The gate commander, Defender of Yuzhou Abuhan Xiehe, had fled. Administrative officer Wanyan Hezhu took temporary command, ordered the guards to release Tashi and the others, and said, "The fault is mine, not yours."

sentences.zh: 」明日，立以數十騎召合住，合住自分必死，易衣冠而往。

translations.literal: The next day Li summoned Hezhu with several tens of horsemen; Hezhu judged he would certainly die and changed his garments before going.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Li summoned Hezhu with several dozen horsemen. Expecting death, Hezhu changed his clothes and went.

sentences.zh: 立左右扼腕欲加刃。

translations.literal: Those beside Li gripped their wrists, ready to apply the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Li's men seized him, blades ready.

sentences.zh: 立遙見，問：「汝是放忠孝軍出門者耶？

translations.literal: Li saw him from afar and asked: "Are you the one who let the Loyal and Filial Army out the gate?"
translations.idiomatic: Li called from a distance, "Are you the man who let the Loyal and Filial Army out the gate?"

sentences.zh: 」合住曰：「然。

translations.literal: Hezhu said: "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhu said, "Yes.

sentences.zh: 天子使命，某實放之，罪在某。

translations.literal: By the Son of Heaven's command I indeed released them; the guilt lies with me."
translations.idiomatic: By the emperor's order I released them. The guilt is mine."

sentences.zh: 」立忽若有所省，顧群卒言：「此官人我識之，前築裏城時與我同事。

translations.literal: Li suddenly seemed to remember something and, turning to the troops, said: "I know this official — when we built the inner wall before, he worked with me.
translations.idiomatic: Li seemed to remember and told his men, "I know this official. When we built the inner wall he worked with me.

sentences.zh: 我所部十餘卒盜官木罪當死，此官人不之問，但笞數十而已。

translations.literal: More than ten soldiers under me stole official timber, a crime deserving death; this official did not prosecute them but only gave several dozen strokes of the rod.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen of my men stole official timber, a capital offense, but he did not prosecute them—only gave them a few dozen strokes.

sentences.zh: 此家能殺人，能救人。

translations.literal: This man can kill and can save lives."
translations.idiomatic: This man can kill, and he can save lives."

sentences.zh: 」因好謂合住曰：「業已放出，吾不汝罪也。」

translations.literal: He then spoke kindly to Hezhu: "They have already been released — I will not blame you."
translations.idiomatic: He then said kindly to Hezhu, "They are already out. I will not punish you."

sentences.zh: 四喜等至歸德，上驚問「兩宮何如？

translations.literal: When Sixi and the others reached Guide, the emperor asked in alarm: "How are the two palaces?
translations.idiomatic: When Sixi and the others reached Guide, the emperor asked in alarm, "How are the two palaces?

sentences.zh: 」二人奏「京城軍變，不及入宮。

translations.literal: The two reported: "There was a military mutiny in the capital; we could not enter the palace."
translations.idiomatic: They reported, "There was a military mutiny in the capital. We could not enter the palace."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「汝父汝妻獨得出耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Only your father and your wife got out?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Only your father and your wife got out?"

sentences.zh: 」下之獄，皆斬於市。

translations.literal: They were cast into prison and all beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: They were thrown into prison and beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：四喜奉迎兩宮，而值崔立之變，智者居此，與兩宮周旋兵間，以俟事變之定而徐圖之。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Sixi was charged to welcome the two palaces but encountered Cui Li's mutiny. A wise man in this situation would move with the two palaces amid the soldiers, waiting for affairs to settle and then planning slowly.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Sixi was sent to welcome the two palaces but met Cui Li's mutiny. A wise man would have stayed with them amid the troops, waited for events to settle, and then planned carefully.

sentences.zh: 萬一不然，以一死徇之耳，他無策也。

translations.literal: If that failed, one would die for the cause — there is no other strategy.
translations.idiomatic: If that failed, the only course was to die for them. There was no other strategy.

sentences.zh: 四喜奉其私親以歸，而望人主貸其死，豈非愚乎！

translations.literal: Sixi brought his private kin home and yet hoped the sovereign would spare his life — is this not folly!
translations.idiomatic: Sixi brought his own kin home and still hoped the emperor would spare him — was that not folly!
